stimulus.text:
“He has kept among us, in times of peace, Standing Armies without the Consent of our legislatures. … He has cut off our Trade with all parts of the world. … He has plundered our seas, ravaged our Coasts, burnt our towns, and destroyed the lives of our people.”
—Declaration of Independence, July 4, 1776 (abridged)
stimulus.source_note: Declaration of Independence, July 4, 1776. Public domain.

source: original; stimulus viewed before writing — Declaration of Independence, July 4, 1776, public domain.

books.section: Topic 3.5 The American Revolution, A. The War for Independence

stem: The grievances listed in the excerpt show that the colonists objected most directly to Britain

options.text: Banning the colonies from trading with France
options.misconception: The grievance is that Britain cut off trade with all parts of the world, not a ban aimed at France in particular.

options.text: Raising taxes on tea and printed paper
options.misconception: Taxes are not listed in this excerpt; the grievances here are standing armies, cut-off trade, and attacks on towns and coasts.

options.text: Using military force and economic pressure without colonial consent
Refusing to allow the colonies to elect a king
options.misconception: The colonies never sought to elect a king; they objected to rule without consent, not to how a king was chosen.

rationales.C: Standing armies in peacetime, trade cut off, seas plundered, and towns burnt are all force used against the colonies without their consent.
rationales.B: Tea and paper taxes are not in this excerpt; the grievances here are armies, trade, and attacks on towns.
rationales.D: The colonists did not want to elect a king; they wanted government by consent, which the grievances say Britain denied them.
rationales.A: The charge is a general cutoff of trade with the world, not a ban on trade with France alone.
rationales.general:
1. List the charges. Standing armies in peacetime, trade cut off, seas plundered, towns burnt.
2. Find the thread. Each charge is Britain using force or economic pressure against people who never consented to it.
3. Rule out the narrower reads. Taxes and France are not in this excerpt, and no one proposed electing a king.
Remember: a list of grievances has a spine — find the one complaint every item shares.
